candidates.title: An Arabic-English Lexicon, entrée بَشِيرٌ
candidates.author: Edward William Lane
candidates.quote: One who announces to a people [or person] an event, either good or evil; but meaning the former oftener than the latter
candidates.supports: Establishes the Arabic meaning of the word bashir. It does not establish that the name is attested in Sudan or that it is non-hereditary there.

candidates.title: Sudan: Knowledge Base profile, version 4.0
candidates.author: HM Passport Office (Home Office)
candidates.quote: Surnames do not exist in Sudan; it is common practice to take the male grandparent's name in place of a surname.
candidates.supports: Supports the non_hereditary_patronymic system and the individual social unit in Sudan. It does not mention the name Bashir.

candidates.title: Côte d'Ivoire : L'ancien Président Henri Konan Bédié s'en est allé à l'âge de 89 ans
candidates.author: Kouamé L.-Ph. Arnaud (Burkina24)
candidates.quote: est né le 5 mai 1934 à Daoukro dans le centre de la Côte d'Ivoire
candidates.supports: Places the one documented bearer in central Côte d'Ivoire. It does not mention the Baoulé people, a clan or the origin of the name, so it does not support clan_name or PPL_BAOULE.

candidates.title: How to quote Ethiopian authors in linguistic publications
candidates.author: Ronny Meyer et Yvonne Treis
candidates.quote: The father's or grandfather's names are not family names but simply given names of the respective individuals.
candidates.supports: Supports nameSystem non_hereditary_patronymic, transmissionMode non_hereditary and designatedSocialUnit individual for Ethiopia. It names Kenenisa Bekele only as an example and says nothing on the meaning of Bekele.
